instruction: I'm working with this spreadsheet and need to export it as a compact PDF that fits on one page. Adjust the cell sizes accordingly and save the PDF in my home directory with the same name as the spreadsheet.

metadata.explanation: Compact export focus. Evaluator checks for proper single-page PDF generation.
metadata.verification_details: Uses existing check_pdf_pages metric to verify: (1) PDF file exists at /home/user/Resize_Cells_Fit_Page.pdf, (2) PDF has exactly 1 page (relation=eq, ref_value=1), (3) PDF file size > 10KB (verify_content=True). No custom functions needed as check_pdf_pages is already available in desktop_env.evaluators.metrics.pdf.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic logic flaw: The check_pdf_pages metric with verify_content=true incorrectly requires PDF to contain raster images (checks for /XObject with /Subtype=/Image at pdf.py:47-58)
Spreadsheet PDFs exported from LibreOffice Calc typically contain text and vector graphics, NOT raster images
The evaluator will incorrectly fail (return 0.0) for valid spreadsheet PDF exports that fulfill all instruction requirements but don't contain raster images
This causes false negatives: a correctly exported single-page spreadsheet PDF will be marked as failed verification
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Remove the image existence check from verify_content logic (pdf.py:46-58), or make it optional
For spreadsheet PDFs, verify_content should only check file size and possibly text extraction, not image presence
Alternative: Change verify_content to false in the evaluator config, relying only on page count and file size checks
Better approach: Implement a spreadsheet-specific content verification that checks for text/table content rather than images

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_pdf_pages first parameter type (str) may not match getter get_vm_file return type (Union)
